title: How to Get a Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)
description: Obtain your annual community tax certificate required for notarization and government permits.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: A government-issued ID such as National ID, Passport, or UMID.

requirements.title: Application Form
requirements.description: A completed Community Tax Declaration Form (CTDF) provided by the local office.

requirements.title: Proof of Income
requirements.description: Payslip, ITR, or Certificate of Employment to determine the additional tax amount.

checklist.title: Prepare Documents
checklist.description: Gather your valid ID and proof of income before visiting the treasurer's office.

checklist.title: Visit City Hall
checklist.description: Proceed to the City or Municipal Treasurer's Office or your local barangay hall.

checklist.title: Fill Out Form
checklist.description: Complete the Community Tax Declaration Form with your personal details and annual income.

checklist.title: Submit Requirements
checklist.description: Present your form and ID to the treasury personnel for computation of your tax.

checklist.title: Pay Community Tax
checklist.description: Pay the basic tax plus any additional tax based on your declared income or property.

checklist.title: Claim Cedula
checklist.description: Receive your signed Community Tax Certificate and verify that all details are correct.

content.title: What is a Community Tax Certificate (Cedula)?

blocks.content: A **Community Tax Certificate (CTC)**, commonly called a **Cedula**, is an official document issued by the local government after payment of the community tax. It serves as proof that an individual or corporation has paid the required community tax for the year.

blocks.content: Individuals aged 18 years old and above who are employed, engaged in business, own property, or are legally required to file taxes may generally obtain a Cedula.
Many government offices request a Cedula before processing permits or applications.
Cedulas are commonly required during notarization and oath-taking procedures.
Applicants for health permits, business permits, and other licenses may need a Cedula.
Although not always accepted as a primary ID, it may support identity verification for certain transactions.

blocks.title: Is a Cedula required for employment?

blocks.content: Many employers and local permit offices still request Cedulas as part of employment or permit requirements.

blocks.title: Can I get a Cedula online?

blocks.content: Most LGUs still require in-person processing, although some cities may offer partial online systems.

blocks.title: How long is a Cedula valid?

blocks.content: Cedulas are generally valid for one calendar year only.

blocks.title: Where should I get my Cedula?

blocks.content: You may usually obtain it from the city or municipality where you reside or where your transaction is being processed.

blocks.title: Is Cedula the same as Barangay Clearance?

blocks.content: No. A Cedula is proof of community tax payment, while Barangay Clearance certifies residency and community standing.
Yes, depending on the purpose and local government requirements.
